sentence_stem: Had the manager listened to the team earlier,
correct_completion: the project would have finished on time.
full_sentence: Had the manager listened to the team earlier, the project would have finished on time.
acceptable_variants: the project would have been completed on time.
we would not have missed the deadline.

options.text: the project would be late now.
options.why_wrong: This describes the present, but the inverted conditional 'Had ... listened' refers to a past situation and needs a past-time consequence.
A future time reference does not match a past hypothetical condition about what could have happened.

options.text: the project would have finished on time.
the team would finish the project.
options.why_wrong: This is a simple conditional, which does not match the past hypothetical set up by 'Had ... listened'.

grammar_focus: Third conditional with inverted 'had' in the if-clause
explanation: The inverted 'Had + subject + past participle' structure replaces 'If + past perfect', so the main clause needs 'would have + past participle'. Speakers whose first language marks hypothetical meaning with a single conditional form often need extra practice with this two-part structure.
translation: Якби менеджер раніше прислухався до команди, проєкт був би завершений вчасно.
